meta.title: Happy Highrise - build a skyscraper, keep everyone moving
meta.description: A pixel-art tower-building game. Pour the floors, let offices, shops, hotels and condos, and keep thousands of simulated people moving - mostly by getting the lifts right. Coming soon to Steam for Windows, macOS and Linux.

preview.text: This site is a private preview of Happy Highrise while it is being built. Nothing is for sale here yet, and there is no Steam page yet.

hero.lede: A tower-building game in pixel art, in the spirit of the 1994 classics. Pour the floors, let the rooms, and get thousands of simulated people where they want to go - mostly by getting the lifts right.

trailer.label: Trailer
trailer.title: One day in the tower
trailer.text: Build it, fill it, move them, earn your stars. Then it goes wrong.
trailer.fallback: Your browser cannot play this video.

floors.label: Build
floors.title: Build it up
floors.text: Start with a lobby on an empty lot. Construction crews pour the floors slab by slab while you fit out offices, shops, restaurants, hotel rooms and condos. Buy more land as the tower grows, and put a crown on the roof when you reach the top.

floors.label: Lifts
floors.title: Everyone needs a lift
floors.text: Every person in your tower is simulated. They arrive on their own schedules, queue, ride, get impatient and leave unhappy. Drag standard, express, service and freight lifts to length, set their dispatch, split them into express bands and add sky lobbies. Rush hour is the test.

floors.label: Utilities
floors.title: Keep the lights on
floors.text: Water pressure from tanks and booster pumps. Power from the grid, the sun, the wind and the basement batteries. Air, refuse, sprinklers. Then the city goes dark, a kitchen catches fire, and it is your building that has to cope.

floors.label: Events
floors.title: Every week, a party
floors.text: Films at the cinema, weddings in the ballroom, an indoor ski hall, snow on the roof and a year-end week in a decorated lobby. A calendar of conferences, tour groups and premieres keeps the tower busy, and the score grows with your star rating.

floors.label: Stars
floors.title: A hundred floors
floors.text: Earn stars from population and satisfaction, confirmed by an inspector who times a real trip through your tower. Spend insight on a research tree, take on scenarios that hand you somebody else's badly built tower, and keep going up.

lobby.label: Lobby
lobby.title: Press and facts
lobby.text: Everything you need to write about the game, in one place.
facts: Rust and Bevy, with a fully deterministic simulation
lobby.kit_text: Logo, store capsules, icons, ten 1920×1080 screenshots and this fact sheet.

dig.label: Underground
dig.title: Then dig down
dig.text: Trucks haul the spoil out, floor by floor, down to B20. Car parks, a nightclub, bunkers, a museum for the ruins you find.
dig.tease: And further down, something nobody told you about.

privacy.title: Privacy
body: This website sets no cookies, runs no analytics or tracking, and loads nothing from anyone else: every font, picture, script and video is served from this site itself. There are no forms, accounts or comments.

The site is hosted on GitHub Pages, a service of GitHub, Inc., 88 Colin P. Kelly Jr. Street, San Francisco, CA 94107, USA. When you open a page, your browser sends the usual request data to GitHub's servers, including your IP address, the page requested, the time and your browser's user agent. GitHub processes this to deliver the site and to keep it secure, and may keep it in server logs. The legal basis is our legitimate interest in delivering a working, secure website (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). GitHub's own policy: GitHub General Privacy Statement.
Links to Steam and other sites take you to their pages, where their own privacy policies apply. Nothing is sent to them until you follow a link.

Under the GDPR you have the right to access, correct, delete and restrict the processing of your personal data, to object to it, and to complain to a data protection supervisory authority. As this site itself stores no personal data, requests about hosting logs are best directed to GitHub. {{privacy_contact}}
